title: SQL Server T-SQL Features and Portability
learningObjectives: Recognize T-SQL row-limiting and identity syntax.
Explain the difference between ISNULL and COALESCE at a high level.
Identify DATEADD, OUTPUT and TRY_CONVERT as SQL Server features.
Use portable CASE and relational query patterns where possible.
Test T-SQL behaviour against the target SQL Server version and compatibility level.

understand.concept: SQL Server uses Transact-SQL (T-SQL), which extends SQL with product-specific data types, procedural features, row-limiting, date functions and DML output clauses.
understand.whyItMatters: T-SQL syntax and behaviour differ from SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL. Explicit dialect labels prevent learners from treating SQL Server extensions as universal SQL.
understand.analogy: A standard road map has local road signs added by a city; drivers need to know which signs belong to that city.
understand.analogyLimit: T-SQL syntax, compatibility level and database settings can change feature availability and behaviour.

explain.narrative:
## Common T-SQL extensions
SQL Server commonly uses `IDENTITY(seed, increment)` for generated values, `TOP (n)` for row limiting, `DATEADD()` for date arithmetic, `OUTPUT inserted...` or `deleted...` to return changed rows, and `TRY_CONVERT()` for safer type conversion.

## NULL fallback functions
SQL Server provides ISNULL and also supports COALESCE. Their type-resolution and return-type rules are not identical in every context; choose deliberately and test the result type.

## Pagination
SQL Server supports `ORDER BY ... OFFSET ... FETCH NEXT ...` for paging. TOP and OFFSET/FETCH require a meaningful order for deterministic results.

## Runnable examples
The examples use SQLite-compatible SQL patterns. SQL Server-only forms are described here as T-SQL references and must be executed against SQL Server to validate their exact behaviour.

examples.title: Create a portable employee table
examples.code: CREATE TABLE dialect23_employees (employee_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, employee_name TEXT NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, salary INTEGER NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: Creates an employee relation. SQL Server commonly uses INT IDENTITY(1,1) for a generated key and NVARCHAR for Unicode text.

examples.title: Insert employee rows
examples.explanation: Adds three employees. In T-SQL, an INSERT with IDENTITY normally omits the identity column unless IDENTITY_INSERT is deliberately enabled.

examples.title: Return the top two salaries in SQLite-compatible syntax
examples.code: SELECT employee_name, salary FROM dialect23_employees ORDER BY salary DESC, employee_id LIMIT 2;
examples.explanation: SQLite uses LIMIT here. The equivalent SQL Server pattern is `SELECT TOP (2) ... ORDER BY salary DESC, employee_id`.

examples.title: Use COALESCE to provide a missing department label
examples.code: SELECT employee_name, COALESCE(department, 'Unassigned') AS department_label FROM dialect23_employees ORDER BY employee_id;
examples.expectedOutput: Asha | Sales; Bilal | Support; Chitra | Sales
examples.explanation: COALESCE is supported by SQL Server and SQLite. SQL Server also provides ISNULL, but its return-type rules can differ from COALESCE.

examples.title: Classify salaries with CASE
examples.code: SELECT employee_name, CASE WHEN salary >= 60000 THEN 'Senior band' ELSE 'Standard band' END AS salary_band FROM dialect23_employees ORDER BY employee_id;
examples.expectedOutput: Asha | Senior band; Bilal | Standard band; Chitra | Senior band
examples.explanation: Uses a portable searched CASE expression. The same business classification can be expressed in T-SQL without relying on a vendor-only function.

practise.guidedTask: Run the examples and rewrite the top-two query using T-SQL TOP. Explain why the ORDER BY must remain present in both forms.
practise.independentTask: Write a T-SQL reference query that uses DATEADD to calculate a due date and OUTPUT inserted values after an update. Label it as SQL Server-only and define a portable alternative.
hints: TOP and IDENTITY are SQL Server syntax.
DATEADD performs date arithmetic in T-SQL.
OUTPUT can return rows changed by DML.
Compatibility level can affect feature availability.

questions.prompt: Which dialect is used by Microsoft SQL Server?
Which syntax limits rows in a common SQL Server query?
questions.explanation: TOP is a common T-SQL row-limiting construct.

questions.prompt: What does DATEADD do in T-SQL?
What does the OUTPUT clause support?
options: Returning rows affected by a DML statement
questions.answer: Returning rows affected by a DML statement
questions.explanation: OUTPUT can expose inserted/deleted row values during DML.

questions.prompt: Why compare ISNULL and COALESCE carefully in SQL Server?
options: Their type-resolution and return-type rules can differ
COALESCE is unsupported in SQL Server
Both always return the same type in every case
questions.answer: Their type-resolution and return-type rules can differ
questions.explanation: Choose based on the expression types and desired result type.
